name: Mundurukú
confidence_why: Picanço 2005, Crofts 1985/2004, Gomes 2006 and Santos 2013 all describe Mundurukú as a tone language, and the only open point is that Crofts's teaching grammar adds a root-final word stress which Picanço's fuller instrumental phonology neither confirms nor denies, so the tonal classification is secure while the stress detail stays unsettled.

new_statements.quote: ACENTO. Acento ocorre quase sempre na última sílaba do radical duma palavra. Quando uma palavra tem mais do que um radical, há acento em cada um. [examples: je'kõn'kõn 'comendo' — acentuados todos dois radicais (radicais duplos); jekiyjo'jõayü 'os ouvintes' (uma radical); imu'piku'pig 'queimando' (dois radicais)] [...] TOM. Há quatro tons em mundurukú. Cada vogal tem um tom "significante". [...] Os quatro tons são relativos, não absolutos. [...] Tom 1, o mais alto, é raro, ocorrendo somente em palavras ou partículas que têm o sentido de 'muito', ou qualquer sentido de superlativo [...] O quarto tom é laringalização.
new_statements.translation: STRESS. Stress occurs almost always on the last syllable of the root of a word. When a word has more than one root, there is stress on each one. [examples: 'eating' — both roots stressed (double roots); 'the listeners' (one root); 'burning' (two roots)] [...] TONE. There are four tones in Mundurukú. Each vowel has a 'significant' tone. [...] The four tones are relative, not absolute. [...] Tone 1, the highest, is rare, occurring only in words or particles that mean 'very' or have any superlative sense [...] The fourth tone is laryngealization.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record (built 2026-09-12 from Picanço 2005) exits as tonal-OR-pitch accent with no stress rule; Crofts (1985 ed.) keeps the language tonal (four 'tons', with laryngealization as tone 4) and ADDS an explicit word-stress statement: root-final, one stress per root. Compatible with the catalog, adds the stress placement. Caveat: this is the first edition, not the listed 2004 second edition; the 2004 text was not obtained.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mundurukú is described as having four lexically significant tones on every vowel (1 super-high/emphatic, 2 high, 3 low, 4 laryngealized), and in addition word stress that falls (almost always) on the final syllable of the root; a word containing two roots (reduplicated or compound stems) carries a stress on each root. Stress is thus positional within the morphological root, not the phonological word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed as such; multi-root words are said to bear a stress on each root (three examples given), which functions like a second stress per root.
new_statements.exceptions: 'quase sempre' (almost always) root-final — exceptions are implied but none are listed. Tone, not stress, is the contrastive feature ('Há muitos pares de palavras que variam somente em tom', p. xvi); relational words and particles (be, dag, gu, ma, juy) alternate between tone 2 and tone 3 by polarity with the preceding tone (p. xvii); tone 2/3 may rise to tone 1 for emphasis or sentence intonation.
new_statements.identity_note: Crofts's grammar was written from sixteen years of fieldwork in the Cururu river villages (Santa Maria, Posto Indígena Mundurukú, Missão São Francisco; acknowledgments p. i), i.e. the Tapajós/Cururu (Pará) variety. Picanço 2005 covers the same main Mundurukú language (dissertation does not, in the sections read, single out a dialect). The Madeira (Amazonas) variety is described separately by Santos 2013, which is held by the project in the same check folder but was not among the listed works.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mundurukú is a lexical tone language with two contrastive levels (H vs L) on the mora as tone-bearing unit (moras lexically H, L, toneless, or carrying a floating H; L-dissimilation, tonal polarity), creaky voice being a vowel feature that co-occurs with L tone; Braun & Crofts's super-high 'accent 1' is reanalysed as a non-contrastive intonational/boundary or emphatic tone (fn. 1, p. 310). tone_statements.quote: No lado fonológico há também a interação com o sistema tonal da língua que restringe a ocorrência de vogais laringalizadas a um tom Baixo. Análises de frequência fundamental demonstram que há uma tendência ao abaixamento na frequência fundamental de vogais laringalizadas, em comparação àquela de vogais modais. ... Essa restrição fonética é refletida na fonologia como uma restrição na realização tonal de uma vogal laringalizada: o tom Baixo.
tone_statements.translation: On the phonological side there is also the interaction with the language's tone system, which restricts the occurrence of laryngealized vowels to a Low tone. Fundamental-frequency analyses show a tendency towards lowering of F0 in laryngealized vowels compared with modal vowels. ... This phonetic restriction is reflected in the phonology as a restriction on the tonal realization of a laryngealized vowel: Low tone.

tone_statements.citation: Mendes Júnior, Djalma Gomes. 2007. Comparação fonológica do Kuruáya com o Mundurukú. Dissertação (Mestrado em Linguística), Universidade de Brasília. 66 f.
tone_statements.quote: O Mundurukú e o Kuruáya são línguas tonais. Braun & Crofts (1965) reconheceram quatro tons em Mundurukú: ‘alto’, ‘médio’, ‘baixo’ e ‘laringalização’. Entretanto, Picanço (2005:12) reconhece um sistema de apenas dois tons contrastivos: Mundurukú is a language that makes use of two levels of pitch, low (L) and high (H), to lexically distinguish items. … toneless moras surface L but this tone is inert. Unstable H and polar tones are the manifestation of a floating H tone. … the tonal system of the language can be reduced to two distinctive levels, rather than the four previously proposed.
tone_statements.translation: Mundurukú and Kuruáya are tone languages. Braun & Crofts (1965) recognised four tones in Mundurukú: 'high', 'mid', 'low' and 'laryngealization'. However, Picanço (2005:12) recognises a system of only two contrastive tones: [English quotation follows as given].
tone_statements.summary: Two contrastive level tones, high and low (following Picanço 2005; earlier four-tone analysis with mid and laryngealization rejected); floating H posited; intensity stress falls on the final syllable.

tone_statements.citation: Picanço, Gessiane Lobato & Denny Moore. 1999. Origem da laringalização em Munduruku. In: Seminário de Iniciação Científica do Museu Goeldi, 7., 1999, Belém. Livro de resumos. Belém: MPEG.
tone_statements.quote: sua estreita relação com a oclusiva glotal e o tom. Os resultados mostram alguns pontos relevantes: (i) sílabas laringalizadas ocorrem sempre com o tom baixo dos dois existentes (Alto e Baixo) no sistema tonal; (ii) oclusiva glotal e laringalização não ocorrem simultaneamente na mesma sílaba; (iii) a oclusiva glotal aparece na superficie antecedendo uma sílaba com tom Alto … (iv) o prefixo de terceira pessoa singular faz com que o tom da sílaba laringalizada inicial do radical de verbo mude para Alto
tone_statements.translation: its close relation to the glottal stop and tone. The results show some relevant points: (i) laryngealized syllables always occur with the low tone of the two existing ones (High and Low) in the tonal system; (ii) glottal stop and laryngealization do not occur simultaneously in the same syllable; (iii) the glottal stop surfaces preceding a syllable with High tone ... (iv) the third person singular prefix makes the tone of the initial laryngealized syllable of the verb root change to High
tone_statements.summary: Two tones, High and Low; creaky syllables always carry Low, a glottal stop surfaces before a High syllable, and the 3sg prefix raises a verb root's first syllable to High. Nothing said on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Picanço, Gessiane Lobato & Denny Moore. 1996. Análise segmental e supra-segmental da língua Mundurukú - tronco Tupi. In: Seminário de Iniciação Científica do Museu Goeldi, 4., 1996, Belém. Livro de resumos. Belém: MPEG.
tone_statements.quote: Juntamente com a formação do GOl'pUS desen-volvia-se não só a investigação segmental como também a determinação dos tons êmicos,já que o informante pode assoviá-Ios perfeitamente. Os resultados obtidos possuem argumentos para, em parte, refutar a análise existente até então (BRAUN & CROFTS, 1969) que versava sobre a existência de quatro tons - tom alto, tom médio, tom baixo e um quarto tom referente à laringalização. Depois de minucioso estudo, constatou-se existirem apenas dois tons - alto e baixo - como é típico das línguas Tupi que sejam tonais.
tone_statements.translation: Along with building the corpus, not only the segmental investigation but also the determination of the emic tones was carried out, since the informant can whistle them perfectly. The results obtained give arguments to refute, in part, the analysis existing until then (BRAUN & CROFTS, 1969), which posited four tones - high tone, mid tone, low tone and a fourth tone referring to laryngealization. After detailed study it was found that only two tones exist - high and low - as is typical of those Tupi languages that are tonal.
tone_statements.locator: sole page of the abstract, body paragraph (no page no.)
tone_statements.summary: Two tones, high and low (an earlier four-tone analysis with mid and 'laryngeal' tones is rejected); laryngealization is not tonal and co-occurs only with low tone. Nothing said on word stress.

readall_conflicts: No direct contradiction on stress, but the two sources that speak to prosody differ in framing. Crofts (1985 ed. of Aspectos, pedagogical grammar, p. xv) describes four lexically significant tones on every vowel (tone 1 super-high/emphatic, 2 high, 3 low, 4 laryngealization) AND a separate word-stress statement: stress almost always on the last syllable of the root, one stress per root in multi-root words. Picanço 2005/2007 (full phonological study) reanalyses the tone system as two levels H/L on the mora with creaky voice as a vowel feature and treats the super-high 'accent 1' as a non-contrastive intonational/emphatic tone (p. 310 fn. 1, p. 311), and never states any word-stress rule; its single mention of stress is that Portuguese loanword stress maps to H tone (p. 120). So Picanço is silent rather than contradictory on stress; Crofts's four-tone inventory versus Picanço's two-level analysis is a difference of analysis of the same pitch facts (Picanço explicitly reports and reanalyses Braun & Crofts / Crofts 1973, 1985). The catalog's existing exit (tonal, no stress rule) stands; Crofts adds a root-final stress statement that the catalog does not yet record. Sheffler's hortatory-discourse paper is silent; Crofts 1973 and Sheffler 1978 could not be opened.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: all deciding passages are verbatim in the Picanço 2005 text we hold at the stated sections and pages (8.1 p. 310 / PDF 324; 8.2 p. 311 / PDF 325; 4.4.2 PDF 134). Deciding source is a 410-pp phonology dissertation with instrumental tone data by the language's main phonologist, the best available and the work every later description defers to. Three open later sources downloaded now (Picanço 2012 teaching monograph pp. 35-36; Santos 2013 UnB MA p. 107; Gomes 2006 UnB PhD pp. 8-9) all state Mundurukú is tonal with two contrastive tones (H/L), laryngealized vowels L-only, and none describes word stress; 'acento' appears only as diacritic names or a generic clitic definition. Web search found no stress/rhythm study or JIPA illustration for Mundurukú. Coding 'tonal', domain not stated by the source, no stress rule, stands. sources.quote: [Introdução, nota 3, PDF p. 9] Há cinco vogais orais (i, , o, e, a) e cinco nasais (ĩ, , õ, ẽ, ã). Ocorre cada sílaba com tom alto, médio ou baixo (indicados pelos números 1, 2, e 3 respectivamente) ou com laringalização (indicada pelo número 4). [...] Para descrição mais detalhada da fonologia e morfofonologia do Munduruku, cf. Braun e Crofts, "Munduruku Phonology", Anthropological Linguistics, 7.7.23-39 (1965). [Apêndice C, 'Explicação de sinais diacríticos', PDF p. 93] Há 4 níveis de tonalidade -- 3 de tom e 1 de laringealização, 1 sendo o mais alto, 2 sendo meio alto, 3 sendo meio baixo e 4 sendo laringealização. sources.quote: [§8.1, p. 310] Braun and Crofts (1965; also Crofts 1973, 1985) analyzed the language as having four opposing tone levels, three of tone and one of laryngealization (i.e. creaky voice) – accent 1 is a super-high tone, accent 2 a high level tone, accent 3 a low level tone, and accent 4 is creakiness. In this chapter (see also Picanço 1997, 2002a-c), I defend the hypothesis that the tone system of Mundurukú can be analyzed as having only two opposing levels: Low and High [...] [§8.2, p. 311] Mundurukú is a tonal language; that is, it makes use of pitch variations to lexically differentiate items. [...] [§4.4.2, p. 120, on Portuguese loans] finally, the Portuguese stressed vowel is reinterpreted as a H-tone vowel.

sources.citation: Picanço, Gessiane Lobato (2012). Introdução ao Mundurukú: fonética, fonologia e ortografia. Cadernos de Etnolingüística, Série Monografias 3. 74 pp.
sources.quote: 'O Mundurukú é uma língua tonal (Braun & Crofts 1965; Picanço 2002, 2005)... A língua possui dois tons contrastivos: o tom Alto (A)... e o tom Baixo (B)... Os únicos segmentos que podem carregar o tom em Mundurukú são as vogais... A forma como os tons A e B serão combinados em uma sequência é imprevisível' (all 4 disyllabic and all 8 trisyllabic H/L patterns attested; laryngealized vowels only L). No word stress/acento de intensidade is described anywhere in the monograph ('acento' occurs only as 'acento agudo/grave' = diacritics).

sources.citation: Sheffler, E. Margaret (1978). Mundurukú discourse. In Papers on discourse. Dallas: SIL. pp. 119-142.
sources.quote: [fn. 1, pp. 119-120 = PDF pp. 129-130] Mundurukú has 17 consonantal phonemes: voiceless stops p, t, c (alveopalatal), k, and ' (glottal stop); voiced stops b, d, and j (alveopalatal); [...] The vowels occur orally and nasalized; i, u (high mid unrounded), o (which phonetically ranges from u to o), e, and a. Each syllable occurs with high, mid, or low pitch, or with laryngealization. Neither pitch nor larnygealization [sic] is symbolized in the practical orthography, except that low pitch is written as ' in inflected verb forms in the third person where it is essential for the differentiation of third from first person. Mundurukú phonology is described more fully by Ilse Braun and Marjorie Crofts: Mundurukú Phonology, Anthropological Linguistics 7:7.23-29 (1965).

sources.quote: ACENTO. Acento ocorre quase sempre na última sílaba do radical duma palavra. Quando uma palavra tem mais do que um radical, há acento em cada um. [examples: je'kõn'kõn 'comendo' — acentuados todos dois radicais (radicais duplos); jekiyjo'jõayü 'os ouvintes' (uma radical); imu'piku'pig 'queimando' (dois radicais)] [...] TOM. Há quatro tons em mundurukú. Cada vogal tem um tom "significante". [...] Os quatro tons são relativos, não absolutos. [...] Tom 1, o mais alto, é raro, ocorrendo somente em palavras ou partículas que têm o sentido de 'muito', ou qualquer sentido de superlativo [...] O quarto tom é laringalização.

sources.quote: No lado fonológico há também a interação com o sistema tonal da língua que restringe a ocorrência de vogais laringalizadas a um tom Baixo. Análises de frequência fundamental demonstram que há uma tendência ao abaixamento na frequência fundamental de vogais laringalizadas, em comparação àquela de vogais modais. ... Essa restrição fonética é refletida na fonologia como uma restrição na realização tonal de uma vogal laringalizada: o tom Baixo.

tone.translation: On the phonological side there is also the interaction with the language's tone system, which restricts the occurrence of laryngealized vowels to a Low tone. Fundamental-frequency analyses show a tendency towards lowering of F0 in laryngealized vowels compared with modal vowels. ... This phonetic restriction is reflected in the phonology as a restriction on the tonal realization of a laryngealized vowel: Low tone.
tone.summary: Tone system (H vs L per Picanço 2005) with creaky vowels restricted to L.
tone.says: Acoustic study of the [constricted glottis] (creaky/laryngealized) vowel contrast and its interaction with the tone system, which restricts laryngealized vowels to Low tone; F0 of creaky vowels is lowered relative to modal vowels, and this phonetic restriction is mirrored phonologically as a constraint that a laryngealized vowel bears L.

sources.citation: Mendes Júnior, Djalma Gomes. 2007. Comparação fonológica do Kuruáya com o Mundurukú. Dissertação (Mestrado em Linguística), Universidade de Brasília. 66 f.
sources.quote: O Mundurukú e o Kuruáya são línguas tonais. Braun & Crofts (1965) reconheceram quatro tons em Mundurukú: ‘alto’, ‘médio’, ‘baixo’ e ‘laringalização’. Entretanto, Picanço (2005:12) reconhece um sistema de apenas dois tons contrastivos: Mundurukú is a language that makes use of two levels of pitch, low (L) and high (H), to lexically distinguish items. … toneless moras surface L but this tone is inert. Unstable H and polar tones are the manifestation of a floating H tone. … the tonal system of the language can be reduced to two distinctive levels, rather than the four previously proposed.
sources.note: Two contrastive level tones, high and low (following Picanço 2005; earlier four-tone analysis with mid and laryngealization rejected); floating H posited; intensity stress falls on the final syllable.

sources.quote: sua estreita relação com a oclusiva glotal e o tom. Os resultados mostram alguns pontos relevantes: (i) sílabas laringalizadas ocorrem sempre com o tom baixo dos dois existentes (Alto e Baixo) no sistema tonal; (ii) oclusiva glotal e laringalização não ocorrem simultaneamente na mesma sílaba; (iii) a oclusiva glotal aparece na superficie antecedendo uma sílaba com tom Alto … (iv) o prefixo de terceira pessoa singular faz com que o tom da sílaba laringalizada inicial do radical de verbo mude para Alto
sources.note: Two tones, High and Low; creaky syllables always carry Low, a glottal stop surfaces before a High syllable, and the 3sg prefix raises a verb root's first syllable to High. Nothing said on stress.

tone.translation: its close relation to the glottal stop and tone. The results show some relevant points: (i) laryngealized syllables always occur with the low tone of the two existing ones (High and Low) in the tonal system; (ii) glottal stop and laryngealization do not occur simultaneously in the same syllable; (iii) the glottal stop surfaces preceding a syllable with High tone ... (iv) the third person singular prefix makes the tone of the initial laryngealized syllable of the verb root change to High

sources.quote: Juntamente com a formação do GOl'pUS desen-volvia-se não só a investigação segmental como também a determinação dos tons êmicos,já que o informante pode assoviá-Ios perfeitamente. Os resultados obtidos possuem argumentos para, em parte, refutar a análise existente até então (BRAUN & CROFTS, 1969) que versava sobre a existência de quatro tons - tom alto, tom médio, tom baixo e um quarto tom referente à laringalização. Depois de minucioso estudo, constatou-se existirem apenas dois tons - alto e baixo - como é típico das línguas Tupi que sejam tonais.

tone.translation: Along with building the corpus, not only the segmental investigation but also the determination of the emic tones was carried out, since the informant can whistle them perfectly. The results obtained give arguments to refute, in part, the analysis existing until then (BRAUN & CROFTS, 1969), which posited four tones - high tone, mid tone, low tone and a fourth tone referring to laryngealization. After detailed study it was found that only two tones exist - high and low - as is typical of those Tupi languages that are tonal.
tone.summary: Two tones, high and low (an earlier four-tone analysis with mid and 'laryngeal' tones is rejected); laryngealization is not tonal and co-occurs only with low tone. Nothing said on word stress.
